correctness.rationale: The quantified extension types over the fixed marked set are a fresh vertex or a mate for a specified currently unpaired marked vertex. A marked host isolate makes its mate type unrealizable, giving zero even with infinitely many edges. Otherwise mates are forced and leave the two resources unchanged. A fresh response either consumes a whole unmarked edge or marks a host isolate, which has successor rank zero; a dangling mate is not fresh. For finite c, induction on the target lower bound and on c for the upper bound give exactly c+1_{d>0}, with the no-fresh-move case zero. Positions without marked host isolates and with infinitely many unused edges admit a response to every type inside the same family; transfinite induction on rank stages therefore gives infinity. Amalgamation holds by identifying the two optional outside mates at each shared unpaired point, if both exist. Unmarking gives the full spectrum, and the labelled edge/set-of-isolates decomposition gives the two EGF factors. Rank r>=1 needs r edges and no isolates or r−1 edges and at least one isolate, proving the minimum, uniqueness up to isomorphism, labelling count, and maximum with fixed n.
residual_risks: The finite enumeration does not establish the countable spectrum; the stable-family argument establishes the infinite-rank case. Rank here is relative to the matching class and over fully fixed marked points.

value.rationale: Matchings form a canonical Fraïssé age with amalgamation but not free amalgamation, so this is a natural case outside the blanket positive Rank Property theorem. The marked law explains why infinitely many isolated vertices do not yield an infinite or transfinite ordinal rank whereas infinitely many edges do. The complete spectrum and labelled census make the example useful for comparison with neighboring rank games, beyond just a negative example for the Rank Property.
residual_risks: No classification of ranks for other extension ages or claimed consequence for unrestricted graphs is needed or established.
